activities.title: Sketch how fatigue feels as a colour
activities.subtitle: Pick a colour that matches how your body feels right now and fill the page slowly. No skill needed.

activities.title: Draw your safe place
activities.subtitle: Sketch a place — real or imagined — where you feel completely safe and calm.

activities.title: Doodle patterns while listening to music
activities.subtitle: Put on a soft playlist and let your hand move without any plan. Fill the page with whatever comes.

activities.title: Draw what hope looks like to you today
activities.subtitle: Hope doesn't have to look pretty. Draw shapes, symbols, or scenes that represent it for you right now.

activities.title: Sketch a window view — real or imagined
activities.subtitle: Draw what you wish you could see outside your window. Let your imagination take you somewhere restorative.

activities.title: Draw every flower you can remember
activities.subtitle: How many flowers can you draw from memory? Roses, daisies, sunflowers — let it become a garden.

activities.title: Sketch your hands
activities.subtitle: Look at your hands and draw them exactly as they are. These hands have carried you through so much.

activities.title: Draw your emotions as weather
activities.subtitle: Is today a storm, a fog, a clearing sky? Draw the weather that matches your emotional state.

activities.title: Blind contour drawing of an object nearby
activities.subtitle: Pick any object close to you. Draw it without looking at the paper. It will look wonderfully strange.

activities.title: Draw the people who love you
activities.subtitle: Sketch the faces or silhouettes of people who have shown up for you. Simple shapes are perfect.

activities.title: Fill a page with soft, circular shapes
activities.subtitle: No corners, no edges. Just slow circles and curves. Let your hand rest as it moves.

activities.title: Sketch something outside your window right now
activities.subtitle: Look outside and draw exactly what you see — tree, rooftop, sky, anything. Observe and capture.

activities.title: Draw what 'rest' looks like
activities.subtitle: What image comes to mind when you think of true rest? A hammock, a quiet room, still water? Draw it.

activities.title: Zentangle — fill a square with repeating patterns
activities.subtitle: Draw a square and fill it with any repeating pattern. Dots, lines, spirals. Repetition is meditative.

activities.title: Draw your cancer journey as a road or path
activities.subtitle: Where did it start? Where are you now? Where does the road go? Draw it however it feels true.

activities.title: Sketch something that made you smile this week
activities.subtitle: Even the smallest thing — a cup of tea, a bird, a message from someone. Draw it as a memory.

activities.title: Free doodle — let your hand move without thinking
activities.subtitle: No goal, no subject. Just let the pen move wherever it wants for 5 minutes.

activities.title: Draw your favourite season
activities.subtitle: Leaves, snowflakes, sunshine, rain — capture the season that makes you feel most like yourself.

activities.title: Draw a mandala — start from the centre out
activities.subtitle: Draw a dot in the middle and add rings of shapes around it. Go as slowly as you need.

activities.title: Portrait of someone you love from memory
activities.subtitle: Draw someone's face from memory — imperfect is perfect. It is the love behind it that counts.

activities.title: Paint your mood using only two colours
activities.subtitle: Pick two colours that reflect how you feel right now. Mix them, layer them, let them tell the story.

activities.title: Watercolour wash — let colours bleed freely
activities.subtitle: Wet the paper and drop different colours onto it. Watch them move and merge on their own.

activities.title: Paint a sunrise or sunset from memory
activities.subtitle: Layer orange, pink, purple, yellow. No photo needed — paint the sky that lives in your memory.

activities.title: Abstract shapes — paint whatever the music makes you feel
activities.subtitle: Put on a song you love and paint shapes, colours, and lines that match what you hear.

activities.title: Paint a tree in your current season of healing
activities.subtitle: Is it bare, budding, or in full bloom? Paint the tree that represents where you are in your journey.

activities.title: Finger painting — no brushes, just touch
activities.subtitle: Use your fingers to spread paint. The direct contact is grounding and deeply sensory.

activities.title: Paint the view from your bed or favourite chair
activities.subtitle: Exactly what you see from where you rest most. Capture this ordinary, precious perspective.

activities.title: Gratitude painting — fill the canvas with things you are thankful for
activities.subtitle: Paint symbols, objects, or people you are grateful for. Let the canvas become a visual thank-you note.

activities.title: Paint the sea — any sea, real or imagined
activities.subtitle: Blue, grey, turquoise, wild or calm — paint a body of water that matches your emotional landscape.

activities.title: Paint your strength — abstract or literal
activities.subtitle: What does your inner strength look like visually? Bold lines, mountain, anchor, flame? Paint it.

activities.title: Monochrome painting — one colour, many shades
activities.subtitle: Pick one colour and explore every shade of it — light to dark. Simple and deeply satisfying.

activities.title: Paint a garden you would love to sit in
activities.subtitle: Flowers, shade trees, a path, a bench — paint the outdoor space that feels most peaceful to you.

activities.title: Splatter painting — controlled chaos on the page
activities.subtitle: Flick paint onto the page. Let it be messy and free. Sometimes you need to make a beautiful mess.

activities.title: Paint something from nature you miss
activities.subtitle: A forest, a beach, a garden, a park you used to walk in. Paint it and let yourself be there for a moment.

activities.title: Paint tonight's sky from memory or imagination
activities.subtitle: Deep blue, scattered stars, moonlight or overcast — paint the sky above you tonight.

activities.title: Paint your favourite food
activities.subtitle: Vivid colours, texture, warmth — paint a meal or food that brings you pure comfort.

activities.title: Abstract colour field — just fill sections with colour
activities.subtitle: Divide the page into sections and fill each one with a different colour that feels right today.

activities.title: Paint a bird in flight
activities.subtitle: One bird, open sky. Freedom and movement painted gently.

activities.title: Paint the last place you felt truly at peace
activities.subtitle: Close your eyes, go there, then open them and paint it from feeling rather than memory.

activities.title: Loose floral painting — imperfect blooms
activities.subtitle: Paint flowers loosely. Overlapping petals, imperfect shapes. Loose and alive is the goal.

activities.title: Body scan from toes to head — notice without judgment
activities.subtitle: Lie still or sit comfortably. Move your attention slowly up your body, noticing sensation without trying to change anything.

activities.title: 5-4-3-2-1 grounding practice
activities.subtitle: Name 5 things you can see, 4 you can touch, 3 you can hear, 2 you can smell, 1 you can taste. Brings you fully into the present.

activities.title: Loving-kindness towards your body
activities.subtitle: Silently repeat: 'May my body be at ease. May my body heal. May my body feel safe.' Let each phrase settle.

activities.title: Visualise a healing light moving through your body
activities.subtitle: Imagine a warm, gentle light entering at the top of your head and slowly moving through every part of you.

activities.title: Counting breath meditation — count to 10, restart
activities.subtitle: Breathe naturally. Count each exhale — 1 through 10 — then start again. When your mind wanders, gently return.

activities.title: Open awareness — notice thoughts without following them
activities.subtitle: Sit quietly and watch thoughts arrive and pass like clouds. You don't need to hold any of them.

activities.title: Gratitude meditation — bring three moments to mind
activities.subtitle: Recall three moments from the last few days you are grateful for. Hold each one for a full breath cycle.

activities.title: RAIN meditation for difficult emotions
activities.subtitle: Recognise what you feel. Allow it to be there. Investigate with kindness. Nurture with self-compassion.

activities.title: Candle or focal point gazing — soften your gaze
activities.subtitle: Focus gently on a candle flame, a point on the wall, or any still object. Let your mind quiet around it.

activities.title: Progressive muscle relaxation — tense and release
activities.subtitle: Starting with your feet, tense each muscle group for 5 seconds, then release. Feel the contrast.

activities.title: Loving-kindness for someone who has supported you
activities.subtitle: Bring someone who has helped you to mind. Silently wish them well. Notice how it feels to give love outward.

activities.title: Sound meditation — just listen without labelling
activities.subtitle: Close your eyes and listen to whatever sounds are present. Don't name them — just receive them as pure sensation.

activities.title: Visualise the end of treatment day
activities.subtitle: Close your eyes and imagine the day treatment ends — who is there, what it feels like, what you do first.

activities.title: Acceptance meditation — 'this is how it is right now'
activities.subtitle: For each difficult thing present in your life, breathe and say: this is how it is right now. Not forever — right now.

activities.title: Brief sitting meditation — just 3 minutes of stillness
activities.subtitle: Set a timer for 3 minutes. Sit comfortably, breathe naturally, and simply be still. Nothing to do, nowhere to go.

activities.title: Walking meditation — slow, deliberate steps indoors
activities.subtitle: Walk very slowly from one side of the room to the other. Feel each foot contact the floor. Repeat.

activities.title: Breath awareness — just notice your natural breath
activities.subtitle: No need to change your breathing. Just observe it. Notice where you feel it most. Follow it for 5 minutes.

activities.title: Morning intention-setting — one word for today
activities.subtitle: Before anything else, sit for a moment and choose one word that will guide today. Rest. Courage. Gentle. Yours to choose.

activities.title: Self-compassion pause — hand on heart
activities.subtitle: Place one hand on your heart, one on your belly. Say to yourself: 'This is hard. I am doing my best. I am not alone.'

activities.title: Evening wind-down body awareness
activities.subtitle: Lie down and notice each part of your body from head to toe. Give each part quiet permission to rest.

activities.title: 5-minute slow walk — count your steps
activities.subtitle: Set a timer for 5 minutes and walk slowly. Count each step. That's it. No distance goal.

activities.title: Walk to the end of the street and back
activities.subtitle: One small loop. Notice three things you haven't looked at carefully before. Movement and observation together.

activities.title: Nature walk — notice every living thing you pass
activities.subtitle: Walk slowly and spot every plant, insect, bird, or growing thing. Let nature's details pull your attention out of your head.

activities.title: Gratitude walk — think of one thing you are grateful for per step
activities.subtitle: With each step, bring one thing to mind that you are grateful for. Small or large. Keep going until you run out of steps first.

activities.title: Walk to somewhere that feels comforting
activities.subtitle: A park bench, a coffee shop, a garden, a friend's house. Walk towards something that feels good.

activities.title: Indoor corridor walk — gentle movement between rooms
activities.subtitle: Walk slowly between rooms in your home. Back and forth. Even 10 minutes of gentle indoor movement counts enormously.

activities.title: Walk after a meal — just 10 minutes
activities.subtitle: A gentle 10-minute walk after eating helps digestion, energy, and mood. Start slowly and let your body lead.

activities.title: Sensory walk — fully notice each of your five senses
activities.subtitle: For each minute of your walk, focus entirely on one sense — sight, sound, touch, smell, taste. Rotate through all five.

activities.title: Walk without a destination — wander freely
activities.subtitle: No route planned. Turn wherever feels right. Reclaim the freedom of aimless movement.

activities.title: Sunrise or sunset walk — time it deliberately
activities.subtitle: Walk during the golden hour. Let the changing light be the point of the whole walk.

activities.title: Walk barefoot on grass or a soft surface
activities.subtitle: If you can, take your shoes off and feel the ground. Grounding through the soles of your feet is deeply calming.

activities.title: Walk with someone — conversation without agenda
activities.subtitle: Ask someone to walk with you. No goal, no plan — just walk and talk or walk in comfortable silence.

activities.title: Photograph walk — capture one beautiful thing
activities.subtitle: Take your phone and walk until you find one thing worth photographing. One image is the whole goal.

activities.title: Stretch walk — stop every 5 minutes and stretch
activities.subtitle: Walk for 5 minutes, stop and stretch your arms, legs, and neck gently. Walk again. Combine movement and release.

activities.title: Celebratory walk — walk because your body can
activities.subtitle: Walk as a celebration of what your body is able to do today. Every step is a small defiance of everything you have been through.

activities.title: Mindful walk around the block — slow and deliberate
activities.subtitle: Walk your block at half your normal pace. There is nowhere to be. Just be here, moving.

activities.title: Morning walk before the day begins
activities.subtitle: Step outside before the day gets busy. Fresh air, quiet streets, soft light. Start the day in your body.

activities.title: Walk after hard news — move the emotion through
activities.subtitle: When feelings are too big to sit with, walk them. Let your legs carry what your mind is holding.

activities.title: Window-shopping walk — look without buying
activities.subtitle: Walk past shops, markets, or storefronts and let yourself enjoy what you see without pressure.

activities.title: Neighbourhood walk — find something new nearby
activities.subtitle: Walk a street you don't usually take. Discover something in your neighbourhood you haven't noticed before.

activities.title: Read one short poem — slowly, twice
activities.subtitle: Find a short poem online or in a book. Read it once for words, once for feeling. Let it land.

activities.title: Read a chapter of something light and escapist
activities.subtitle: A novel, a travel memoir, a feel-good story — something that takes you entirely somewhere else for 20 minutes.

activities.title: Read one page of a book you haven't opened in a while
activities.subtitle: Open a book you left half-read. Just one page — no commitment. Reconnect with a story waiting for you.

activities.title: Read a cancer survivor's story — find someone who came through
activities.subtitle: A memoir, a blog post, a short interview. Let someone else's 'I made it' be something you hold onto today.

activities.title: Read about a place you would love to visit
activities.subtitle: Travel writing, a Wikipedia page, a blog post — let yourself dream about somewhere beautiful while your body rests.

activities.title: Reread something you loved years ago
activities.subtitle: A childhood book, an old favourite novel, a treasured story. Let familiarity be comfort.

activities.title: Read a short story start to finish in one sitting
activities.subtitle: A complete short story — 15 to 30 minutes. The satisfaction of finishing something matters right now.

activities.title: Read letters or essays written to people facing illness
activities.subtitle: Letters of hope written to patients, essays on healing, thoughtful personal writing. Others have walked this path.

activities.title: Read something funny — humour as medicine
activities.subtitle: A comic strip, a funny essay, a humorous book. Laughter does something real to the body. Give yourself permission.

activities.title: Read about the science of healing and recovery
activities.subtitle: A book or article about how the body heals. Understanding what is happening can make it feel less frightening.

activities.title: Read a nature book or wildlife essay
activities.subtitle: Something about birds, forests, oceans, or animals. Nature writing is deeply calming and completely absorbing.

activities.title: Read a cookbook — just browse, no cooking required
activities.subtitle: Flick through recipes, look at photos, imagine making things. The pleasure of food without any effort.

activities.title: Read quotes about courage and survival
activities.subtitle: Collect three to five quotes that feel true to what you are going through. Write down the one that hits hardest.

activities.title: Read a magazine or browse something purely visual
activities.subtitle: A photography magazine, a design blog, an art book. Images with words. Low demand, high pleasure.

activities.title: Read the next chapter of whatever you're currently reading
activities.subtitle: Don't think about it — just pick up your current book and read the next chapter. Simple and satisfying.

activities.title: Browse a subject you have always been curious about
activities.subtitle: Pick something you've always wanted to know more about and spend 20 minutes reading about it. Curiosity is energising.

activities.title: Read in bed — let it be the whole activity
activities.subtitle: Get comfortable, get your book, and let reading be enough. Not a precursor to sleep — an activity in itself.

activities.title: Read a children's book — revisit simple wonder
activities.subtitle: A picture book or short illustrated story. Simple language, beautiful images, gentle wisdom. No age requirement for comfort.

activities.title: Read one essay or long-form article about something you care about
activities.subtitle: A well-written piece on something that genuinely interests you. Give it your full attention for 15–20 minutes.

activities.title: Read outside, or near an open window
activities.subtitle: Take your book somewhere with fresh air. The combination of reading and open air is restorative.

activities.title: Create a 'chemo playlist' of your most comforting songs
activities.subtitle: Build a playlist specifically for treatment days. Songs that feel like a hand on your shoulder.

activities.title: Listen to classical music with your eyes closed
activities.subtitle: Choose a slow orchestral piece — Debussy, Satie, Bach. Let the music be the only thing happening.

activities.title: Listen to nature sounds — rain, forest, ocean
activities.subtitle: Find a nature soundscape and let it play. Close your eyes and let the sound take you somewhere natural.

activities.title: Listen to the album that defined a happy period of your life
activities.subtitle: Pick an album from a time when life felt good. Let the music return you to a version of yourself that was whole.

activities.title: Listen to binaural beats or healing frequency music
activities.subtitle: Search for 528Hz or theta wave music. Lie down with headphones and let the frequency work on your nervous system.

activities.title: Listen to music from your childhood — nostalgia as comfort
activities.subtitle: Songs from school, family road trips, holidays. Let familiar music reconnect you to a self that existed before all this.

activities.title: Listen to a gentle film score — music without words
activities.subtitle: Film scores from Studio Ghibli, Hans Zimmer, or Ennio Morricone. Emotional, beautiful, no lyrics to process.

activities.title: Create a playlist for the person you are becoming
activities.subtitle: Songs that represent where you want to be — after treatment, in recovery, fully yourself again. A musical vision board.

activities.title: Listen to music while doing a slow hand massage
activities.subtitle: Put on a soft playlist and slowly massage your own hands and wrists. Combine sound with touch.

activities.title: Choose one song and listen to it three times in a row
activities.subtitle: Pick a song that matches your mood. Listen to it start to finish three times. Let yourself fully inhabit it.

activities.title: Listen to a podcast about music or an artist you love
activities.subtitle: Not just music — but a conversation about music. Something engaging that keeps your mind gently company.

activities.title: Listen to lo-fi or ambient music while resting
activities.subtitle: Put on lo-fi hip hop, ambient, or soft electronic music. No peaks, no lyrics. Just texture to rest inside.

activities.title: Listen to cultural or world music from a place that means something to you
activities.subtitle: Music rooted in a culture or place connected to your history, family, or travels. Let it root you.

activities.title: Listen to a guided relaxation set to music
activities.subtitle: Find a guided relaxation or sleep story with background music. Let a voice and melody carry you to rest.

activities.title: Listen and notice — what memory does this song bring up?
activities.subtitle: Let a song play and notice what it brings to mind. A person, a place, a feeling. Sit with what comes.

activities.title: Put on a soft playlist and just rest without screens
activities.subtitle: Music on, phone face down, eyes closed or soft-focused. Nothing else. Just you and the sound.

activities.title: Listen to your favourite song when you need a lift
activities.subtitle: The one song that always works. Play it. Let it do what it does.

activities.title: Morning music ritual — same soft song every morning
activities.subtitle: Choose one calming song as your daily anchor. The same song each morning creates a gentle ritual of continuity.

activities.title: Listen to instrumental jazz — background warmth
activities.subtitle: Soft jazz piano or trio. It fills the room with warmth without demanding your attention.

activities.title: Make a playlist for someone you love
activities.subtitle: Curate a playlist as a gift for someone important to you. A private act of love that also nourishes you.

activities.title: Make ginger tea from scratch — steep and sip slowly
activities.subtitle: Grate fresh ginger into hot water with honey and lemon. Hold the warm cup and drink it slowly. Ginger actively helps nausea.

activities.title: Cook a simple soup — just stock, vegetables, warmth
activities.subtitle: Warm broth with soft vegetables. Easy on the stomach, deeply nourishing. Let the process be slow and meditative.

activities.title: Bake something simple — banana bread or plain muffins
activities.subtitle: The rhythm of mixing, the smell of baking, the result you can share. Low complexity, high reward.

activities.title: Make a blended smoothie with healing ingredients
activities.subtitle: Blend banana, ginger, turmeric, and coconut milk. Gentle on the stomach, easy to make, anti-inflammatory.

activities.title: Cook your comfort food — whatever feels like home
activities.subtitle: The meal that means comfort. Make it exactly as you remember. Let the cooking be a form of self-care.

activities.title: Make herbal tea and document how each one feels
activities.subtitle: Chamomile, peppermint, lemon balm, rooibos. Brew them one at a time and notice how each feels in your body.

activities.title: Prepare a meal as a gift for someone who has helped you
activities.subtitle: Cook something and give it away. Feeding someone else is a profound act that also fills you.

activities.title: Try one new anti-inflammatory recipe
activities.subtitle: Turmeric, leafy greens, berries, olive oil. Find one simple recipe using ingredients known to support recovery.

activities.title: Make something from a recipe that belonged to someone you love
activities.subtitle: A grandmother's dish, a family recipe, a meal from your childhood. Cook as a way of being close to them.

activities.title: Make a nourishing breakfast entirely for yourself
activities.subtitle: Warm oats, poached eggs, fresh fruit — whatever nourishes you most. Cook it slowly and eat it without rushing.

activities.title: Prepare a meal using only soft textures — easy on the body
activities.subtitle: Mashed, steamed, or blended. When mouth sores or nausea are present, soft food made with care is medicine.

activities.title: Make a warming spiced drink — golden milk or chai
activities.subtitle: Turmeric milk, cinnamon chai, or spiced cocoa. Warming, aromatic, and deeply soothing.

activities.title: Cook something colourful — eat with your eyes first
activities.subtitle: Roasted vegetables, a colourful salad, a vivid bowl. When appetite is low, visual appeal helps the first bite.

activities.title: Try batch cooking for rest days ahead
activities.subtitle: Make a double portion today and store the rest. Future you will be grateful. A small act of self-care across time.

activities.title: Make ice cubes with fruit or mint to help with nausea
activities.subtitle: Freeze small cubes of lemon, mint, or ginger in water. Sucking on them helps with treatment-related nausea and dry mouth.

activities.title: Make your favourite hot drink and sit with it intentionally
activities.subtitle: Whatever your drink is — make it the right way, cup it in your hands, and drink it slowly without anything else happening.

activities.title: Prepare a simple one-pot meal — minimum effort, maximum nourishment
activities.subtitle: One pot, a few ingredients, 20 minutes. You deserve to eat well without it costing you energy you don't have.

activities.title: Cook while listening to a podcast or audiobook
activities.subtitle: Combine two gentle activities. Let cooking become a background activity while your mind is entertained.

activities.title: Make something sweet — a small treat entirely for you
activities.subtitle: A few cookies, a small cake, a chocolate pudding. You are allowed sweetness. Make it and enjoy every bite.

activities.title: Follow a new recipe step by step — focus on the process
activities.subtitle: Pick a recipe you have never made. Read each step carefully and follow it exactly. Let the process absorb you.

activities.title: Call someone and ask them to just listen — no advice needed
activities.subtitle: Tell them before you start: I just need you to listen right now. Then say what is really on your mind.

activities.title: Tell someone one specific thing they did that helped you
activities.subtitle: Name it clearly. Not 'thanks for everything' — but 'when you did that specific thing, it helped me in this specific way.'

activities.title: Video call someone you haven't spoken to in a while
activities.subtitle: Isolation during treatment can drift into distance. Reach out to someone you miss — a face on a screen helps.

activities.title: Ask someone to share a happy memory with you
activities.subtitle: Call someone close and ask: tell me about a happy memory you have. Then just listen. Let their past warm you.

activities.title: Tell your family what you need this week — specifically
activities.subtitle: Not 'I need support' — but 'I need someone to bring dinner on Thursday' or 'I need an hour of quiet company.' Specific asks help.

activities.title: Share how treatment is really going — not the edited version
activities.subtitle: Tell someone the unfiltered truth about how you are feeling. Not to protect them. For once, let them hold the real version.

activities.title: Have a conversation about something completely unrelated to illness
activities.subtitle: Ask about their week, a show they are watching, something ordinary. Let yourself be in a normal conversation for once.

activities.title: Write a voice note to someone you haven't been able to call
activities.subtitle: If a phone call feels like too much, record a voice message instead. Your voice reaching them still matters.

activities.title: Tell someone you love them — plainly and directly
activities.subtitle: Text, call, or say it in person. Three words. Simple, direct, and always worth saying now.

activities.title: Share one fear you have been carrying alone
activities.subtitle: Pick one person who can hold it without panicking. Say: I have been afraid of something I haven't told you. Then say it.

activities.title: Ask someone to come and simply be with you — no agenda
activities.subtitle: Ask someone to come over or stay on a video call without any plan. Just presence. Shared silence counts.

activities.title: Call a family member who has been through something hard themselves
activities.subtitle: Reach out to someone who knows what difficulty feels like. Let them remind you they came through it. You will too.

activities.title: Plan something to look forward to with someone you love
activities.subtitle: Name a future moment together — a meal, a trip, a visit. Having something to look forward to genuinely helps.

activities.title: Have a conversation about something funny — share a memory that makes you both laugh
activities.subtitle: Ask: what's the funniest memory you have of us? Let laughter be the whole point of the call.

activities.title: Ask someone to read something to you
activities.subtitle: A chapter of a book, a poem, an article. Ask them to read while you close your eyes and just receive it.

activities.title: Message someone to check in — ask how they are doing too
activities.subtitle: Sometimes reaching outward — genuinely asking how someone else is — takes you momentarily out of your own pain.

activities.title: Share something you are proud of with someone who loves you
activities.subtitle: Something you have done, endured, or handled. Say: I wanted to tell you I'm proud of myself for this.

activities.title: Send a voice message instead of a text today
activities.subtitle: Your voice carries more than words. Record what you want to say and send it. Let someone hear you.

activities.title: Call someone just to say you were thinking of them
activities.subtitle: No agenda. Just: I was thinking of you and wanted to hear your voice. That's it.

activities.title: Watch the same TV show together over video call
activities.subtitle: Sync up on a show and watch it together remotely. Shared experience without needing to talk.

activities.title: Repot a houseplant that has outgrown its pot
activities.subtitle: A slow, grounding task. New soil, new space — tending to growth when your own feels uncertain.

activities.title: Plant seeds and commit to watching them grow
activities.subtitle: Sow some seeds — herbs, flowers, vegetables. Tend to something that grows in time with your recovery.

activities.title: Care for your houseplants — water, dust leaves, check soil
activities.subtitle: A quiet indoor ritual. Look at each plant. Water the ones that need it. Wipe the dust from their leaves.

activities.title: Deadhead flowers and encourage new blooms
activities.subtitle: Remove spent flowers to help the plant redirect energy to new growth. A gentle metaphor you can feel.

activities.title: Grow something edible on a windowsill — herbs, lettuce, microgreens
activities.subtitle: A small pot on a sunny ledge. Watching something edible grow that you can later use to nourish yourself.

activities.title: Sit in your garden or a park and observe without doing
activities.subtitle: No weeding, no planting — just sit outside and watch. A bee, a bird, a cloud, the wind in the leaves.

activities.title: Press flowers and create a simple pressed flower page
activities.subtitle: Collect a few flowers, press them between heavy books. In a week, you will have something beautiful to keep.

activities.title: Create a small terrarium or moss garden in a jar
activities.subtitle: Layer stones, soil, and moss in a glass jar. A tiny self-contained world to keep by your bedside.

activities.title: Visit a botanical garden or flower market
activities.subtitle: Surround yourself with green living things. Even one hour among plants and flowers is restorative.

activities.title: Buy yourself one flower — one single stem
activities.subtitle: Buy a flower just for yourself. Put it in a glass of water where you will see it. You are worth one flower.

activities.title: Learn about one plant you already own
activities.subtitle: Look up the history, origin, and meaning of one plant in your home. Where does it come from? What does it mean?

activities.title: Tend to an outdoor herb garden or container garden
activities.subtitle: Trim, water, harvest a few leaves. The smell of fresh herbs is grounding in a way that is hard to explain.

activities.title: Read about the meaning of flowers — create a bouquet in your mind
activities.subtitle: Look up the symbolism of different flowers. If you could send someone a bouquet today, what would it say?

activities.title: Propagate a plant from a cutting
activities.subtitle: Snip a stem, place it in water, wait. Watching roots appear over days is quietly miraculous.

activities.title: Write plant care notes for each of your houseplants
activities.subtitle: Document what each plant needs — light, water, temperature. A gentle act of stewardship and attention.

activities.title: Water your plants and talk to them
activities.subtitle: It sounds strange but it works. Talk to your plants as you water them. Say whatever is on your mind.

activities.title: Put a plant outside for fresh air and bring it back in
activities.subtitle: Even houseplants benefit from a spell of outdoor air. Move one outside for a few hours. A small act of care.

activities.title: Arrange flowers from a garden or market into a simple vase
activities.subtitle: A loose, imperfect arrangement. Nothing formal. Just bringing life and colour into the room.

activities.title: Clear a small patch of weeds — the satisfaction of tidying
activities.subtitle: Pick one small, manageable patch. Clear it out. The physical result is immediate and satisfying.

activities.title: Photograph your plants and notice how they have changed
activities.subtitle: Look at your plants carefully and photograph them. Compare to old photos if you have them. Growth takes time.

activities.title: Make a paper chain of things you are grateful for
activities.subtitle: Write one thing per strip of paper and link them into a chain. Hang it somewhere you can see it.

activities.title: Create a vision board with magazine cutouts
activities.subtitle: Cut out words, images, and colours that represent what you want after treatment. Let the future feel real.

activities.title: Fold origami — start with a simple crane or flower
activities.subtitle: Origami requires focused hands and a quieted mind. The repetition is meditative. Start with a crane.

activities.title: Make a friendship bracelet or simple woven band
activities.subtitle: Three threads, a simple knot pattern, 15 minutes. Make it for yourself or someone who has supported you.

activities.title: Create a photo collage of people and places you love
activities.subtitle: Print or arrange phone photos of your favourite people and moments. A physical reminder of what you are holding onto.

activities.title: Knit or crochet one small square — no project needed
activities.subtitle: Cast on 20 stitches and knit one small square. The rhythm of knitting is one of the most calming repetitive motions.

activities.title: Make greeting cards for people who have supported you
activities.subtitle: Simple folded paper, a written message, a small drawing. A handmade card says more than anything bought.

activities.title: Create a paper flower bouquet — no watering required
activities.subtitle: Fold or cut paper into simple flower shapes. Make a bunch of them in colours that lift your mood.

activities.title: Decorate a notebook that will become your journal
activities.subtitle: Personalise the cover with stickers, washi tape, or drawings. Make it yours before you write a single word inside.

activities.title: Make a worry jar — write worries on paper and fold them inside
activities.subtitle: Write each worry on a small strip of paper, fold it, put it in a jar. Externalising worry physically reduces its power.

activities.title: Make a simple bookmark — a small, useful creation
activities.subtitle: Cut and decorate a strip of card. Something functional you made yourself. Small craft, complete satisfaction.

activities.title: Embroider or cross-stitch a simple pattern
activities.subtitle: A flower, a word, a simple shape. Needle and thread on fabric. Slow, deliberate, meditative.

activities.title: Make a scrapbook page of a happy memory
activities.subtitle: One page. Photos, tickets, notes, drawings. A single memory preserved with care.

activities.title: Build something with clay or air-dry dough
activities.subtitle: Knead, shape, sculpt. The physical working of clay with your hands is deeply grounding and stress-relieving.

activities.title: Make a nature-inspired craft — pressed leaves, pebble painting
activities.subtitle: Collect leaves, pebbles, or twigs and use them in a simple craft. Bring the outside in.

activities.title: Washi tape a notebook, frame, or surface — a small decorating project
activities.subtitle: Washi tape is forgiving, colourful, and satisfying. Decorate something small and make it feel new.

activities.title: Tear paper into shapes and create a collage
activities.subtitle: No scissors needed. Tear coloured paper into organic shapes and arrange them into something. Tearing can be therapeutic.

activities.title: Create something using only what you have at home
activities.subtitle: Rubber bands, string, paper clips, cardboard. What can you make from only what is around you right now?

activities.title: Bead a simple bracelet — sort the colours, string them slowly
activities.subtitle: Sorting and stringing beads is repetitive, calming, and ends with something wearable.

activities.title: Make something and give it away today
activities.subtitle: A folded card, a drawing, a bracelet — make something simple and give it to whoever is nearby. Creating for others is deeply satisfying.

activities.title: Watch a nature documentary — let the world be big and beautiful
activities.subtitle: Planet Earth, Our Planet, Blue Planet. When your world is small, let the screen fill it with vast, living nature.

activities.title: Rewatch a childhood film that made you happy
activities.subtitle: A film you loved when you were young. Comfort, nostalgia, and a reminder of who you were before all this.

activities.title: Watch a film set in a beautiful location you dream of visiting
activities.subtitle: Italy, Japan, New Zealand, Scotland — let the landscape take you somewhere gorgeous while you rest.

activities.title: Watch a comedy you have already seen — laugh without effort
activities.subtitle: A film you know is funny. No surprises, no demands — just comfortable laughter you know is coming.

activities.title: Watch a film about someone who overcame something enormous
activities.subtitle: A true story of survival, resilience, or triumph. Let someone else's story remind you what human beings can do.

activities.title: Watch a short film — complete something in 20 minutes
activities.subtitle: Find a short film online. Something complete and finished in 20 minutes. The satisfaction of a whole story.

activities.title: Watch a cooking or baking show — food as comfort television
activities.subtitle: The Great British Bake Off, Chef's Table, Salt Fat Acid Heat. Food, warmth, and gentle competition.

activities.title: Watch a travel documentary about somewhere you have never been
activities.subtitle: Let yourself travel without leaving your bed. Somewhere completely different. New landscapes, new cultures.

activities.title: Watch a film you have been putting off for years
activities.subtitle: The one on your list you keep postponing. Today is the day. A film that has been waiting for you.

activities.title: Watch a musical — let music and story carry you together
activities.subtitle: Hamilton, Mamma Mia, The Greatest Showman, La La Land. Music, colour, and story combined.

activities.title: Watch a documentary about art, music, or creativity
activities.subtitle: A film about an artist, a band, a photographer. Creative lives are energising and absorbing to watch.

activities.title: Watch a gentle romance — let yourself feel something warm
activities.subtitle: A love story with warmth and hope. Let the feeling it gives you exist alongside everything else.

activities.title: Watch a film in another language — fully read the subtitles
activities.subtitle: A French film, a Korean drama, an Italian classic. Let another culture's storytelling world in.

activities.title: Watch something you watched with someone you love
activities.subtitle: A film tied to a specific memory with a specific person. Watch it and let yourself feel that connection.

activities.title: Watch a wildlife or animal documentary — pure comfort viewing
activities.subtitle: Dogs, octopuses, lions, penguins. Animals doing extraordinary things. Uncomplicated and deeply enjoyable.

activities.title: Continue a series you have been watching
activities.subtitle: Pick up where you left off. The comfort of a continuing story and characters you already know.

activities.title: Watch something funny — just pure laughter tonight
activities.subtitle: A stand-up special, a sitcom, a comedy film. Laughter is medicine. Give yourself full permission.

activities.title: Start a new series someone you love recommended
activities.subtitle: Text them: I'm watching it tonight. Watch the first episode and message them what you think.

activities.title: Watch with snacks — make it an experience, not just background
activities.subtitle: Make a small plate of something good. Set up properly. Turn watching into an intentional, comfortable event.

activities.title: Watch a classic film you have always meant to see
activities.subtitle: An acknowledged masterpiece you have never watched. Tonight is the night. A cultural experience waiting for you.

activities.title: Play or hum a song from your childhood
activities.subtitle: At an instrument or just with your voice. A song from childhood carries comfort that bypasses the thinking mind.

activities.title: Improvise freely on an instrument — no rules, no wrong notes
activities.subtitle: Play whatever comes. No scales, no songs. Let the instrument become a voice for what you are feeling.

activities.title: Learn one new chord or note on an instrument
activities.subtitle: If you play something, learn just one new thing today. One chord, one melody line. A tiny step forward.

activities.title: Sing a song you love loudly — alone in the house
activities.subtitle: When no one is listening, sing as loudly as you want to a song that means something. Singing releases as much as crying.

activities.title: Play the same piece or song you already know, slowly and intentionally
activities.subtitle: Not to perform — to inhabit. Play something familiar much more slowly than usual. Hear every note.

activities.title: Use a drum pad, table, or kitchen to create a rhythm
activities.subtitle: Tap a rhythm on your table, legs, or a drum pad. Rhythm is grounding. You don't need an instrument.

activities.title: Record yourself playing or singing — just once
activities.subtitle: Record a short clip on your phone. Not to share — just to hear yourself. Your voice and music, documented.

activities.title: Whistle or hum while doing another gentle activity
activities.subtitle: Hum while you make tea, water plants, or get comfortable. Continuous humming calms the vagus nerve.

activities.title: Play the first song you ever learned on an instrument
activities.subtitle: Whatever it was — one finger on a keyboard, a simple chord. Return to the beginning. There is comfort there.

activities.title: Try a simple music app or virtual keyboard if no instrument available
activities.subtitle: GarageBand, a piano app, a virtual drum kit. Make sound on your phone. Music doesn't require an instrument.

activities.title: Play a lullaby or soothing melody very softly
activities.subtitle: Something slow and tender. Play it for yourself the way you might for a child who needs soothing.

activities.title: Write one line of a song about where you are right now
activities.subtitle: Not a whole song — just one honest line. What would the first line of your song be today?

activities.title: Play along with a recording of a song you love
activities.subtitle: Play your instrument alongside a recording. Even rough, imperfect harmony with music you love is joyful.

activities.title: Clap, tap, and feel a rhythm move through your body
activities.subtitle: Feel a beat physically. Tap your knees, clap softly, let the rhythm work through you. Movement and music, minimal effort.

activities.title: Look up tabs or chords for a song you have always wanted to learn
activities.subtitle: Find the chords for one song. Learn just the first four bars. Start the thing you have been putting off.

activities.title: Play whatever you feel like for 10 minutes — completely freely
activities.subtitle: No structure, no goal. Just play for 10 minutes. Let whatever is inside find its way out through sound.

activities.title: Hum while you breathe deeply — a simple toning practice
activities.subtitle: Breathe in, and hum on the exhale. The vibration in your chest is calming and physically soothing.

activities.title: Sing in the shower — the most accessible stage
activities.subtitle: The acoustics are perfect. No audience. Sing whatever you want as long or as short as you like.

activities.title: Listen to a song and figure out the chords by ear
activities.subtitle: Put on a simple song and try to work out the chords by ear on any instrument. Engaging and satisfying.

activities.title: Play or sing something for someone you love over the phone
activities.subtitle: Call someone, play or sing them something short. The most personal and direct gift you can give.

activities.title: Write a letter to your body — thank it, argue with it, or just check in
activities.subtitle: Address your body directly. Tell it how you feel about what it is going through. Say what you haven't been able to say.

activities.title: Write a letter to cancer — say everything you have wanted to say to it
activities.subtitle: Anger, grief, defiance, exhaustion — write the letter you can't send. Address it directly.

activities.title: Write about the person you are becoming through this
activities.subtitle: Not who you were before, not who you want to be — but who you are in the process of becoming right now.

activities.title: Record three things that happened today — just the facts
activities.subtitle: Not feelings, not analysis — just three things that happened. Ground yourself in the concrete reality of the day.

activities.title: Write a list of 10 things you still want to do
activities.subtitle: Big or small, near or far. Wants. Things that exist beyond treatment. Let yourself want things again.

activities.title: Write freely for 5 minutes — no editing, no stopping
activities.subtitle: Set a timer and write continuously. Don't lift the pen. Don't re-read. Just keep going. Let the subconscious speak.

activities.title: Write about a specific day from before your diagnosis
activities.subtitle: Choose an ordinary day that feels precious in retrospect. Describe it in full detail. Bring it back.

activities.title: Write a gratitude list — at least 10 items, no matter how small
activities.subtitle: Push past the obvious ones. Fresh water. A soft pillow. The ability to breathe. A friend who texted. Keep going.

activities.title: Write about the best day you can remember
activities.subtitle: Not an important day — the best day. What made it the best? Who was there? What did your body feel like?

activities.title: Write to your future self — one year from today
activities.subtitle: What do you hope they are doing? What do you want them to remember about now? Write across time.

activities.title: Write about what strength means to you now versus before
activities.subtitle: Has your definition of strength changed? What looks strong to you now that didn't before?

activities.title: Write a list of people who have shown up for you — and what they did
activities.subtitle: Name each person and the specific thing they did. The act of naming and recording generosity is powerful.

activities.title: Write a description of your ideal recovery day
activities.subtitle: Paint the picture fully — where you are, who is there, what you are doing, how your body feels. Make it vivid.

activities.title: Write about what the hardest moment so far has taught you
activities.subtitle: Not to silver-line it — but to honestly examine what the hardest thing has given you that you didn't ask for.

activities.title: Write one sentence that is completely, uncomplicatedly true today
activities.subtitle: One sentence. It can be tiny or enormous. Just: one true thing about today.

activities.title: Write the story of your diagnosis day — as if telling a stranger
activities.subtitle: Describe that day from a slight distance. What happened? Who called? Where were you? What was the first thing you did?

activities.title: Make a list of everything you want to say thank you for
activities.subtitle: To people, to experiences, to your own body for fighting. A list of thank-yous without needing to send them.

activities.title: Write about a relationship that has changed since your diagnosis
activities.subtitle: Better, harder, different, absent. How has one significant relationship shifted? What do you feel about that?

activities.title: Write what you want people to know about your experience
activities.subtitle: Not what you say when they ask. What you actually want them to know. Write it for no audience but yourself.

activities.title: Write about a small moment of beauty you witnessed today
activities.subtitle: Light through a window, a kind gesture, a flower, a memory. Something beautiful that exists alongside the hard.
